clue.text: It is popular on television but it makes one snore horribly if not all right

indicators.note: done horribly, the letters of the word snore are mangled into a new order

parts.note: OK is short for all right

explanation.surface: A televised game so dull it sends a viewer to sleep, snoring badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: take OK ('all right') out of the answer and what remains, rearranged ('horribly'), is SNORE; so SNORE scrambled with OK makes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The cue-sports game was a staple of British television viewing, drawing huge audiences.

clue.text: Wicked person who may be rescued if converted

indicators.note: converted letters are changed into another form, a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A villain who might be saved if he found religion.
explanation.definitionFit: One who leads others astray, especially sexually, is a wrongdoer.

clue.text: There is nothing in having music on the box — performance is all

definitions.text: There is nothing in having music on the box — performance is all

parts.words: There is nothing in having music on the box — performance is all
parts.note: reads like a remark about television, but describes simply working a device or carrying out a procedure

explanation.definitionFit: Working a machine or carrying out a procedure is a performance of it.

clue.text: Kent left in obscurity although got ready to be knighted

indicators.note: with things obscured and muddled, the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man of Kent, little known, nonetheless prepared for his knighthood.
explanation.definitionFit: One kneels to be dubbed a knight, so going down on one knee is getting ready.

clue.text: It is used by Catholics for a woman without a right

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: Rosy is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Something Catholics use for a woman who lacks a right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: ROSY goes round A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A string of prayer beads is the Catholic aid for counting prayers.

clue.text: Call the evidence of debts uncertain

parts.note: to dub is to call or name
IOUs are written notes acknowledging debts

explanation.surface: Someone describes their proof of money owed as shaky.
explanation.definitionFit: Something doubtful or questionable is not certain.

clue.text: Am embraced by one who eats little, but the round figure has it

indicators.note: something embraced is held inside another

parts.note: a dieter eats less

explanation.surface: A slimmer hugs someone, but the plump one has the edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round figure' sounds like a plump body but means a circle, which has a diameter.
explanation.definitionFit: A circle has a line across its centre whose length measures its width.

clue.text: The hungry are born to get through fewer books

parts.note: to read books is to get through them
less means fewer

explanation.surface: Starving people manage to read fewer books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'books' only completes the sense of READ and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without food or a loaf means going hungry.

clue.text: Loud in tone, modified in frequency

definitions.note: the definition is a noun; the answer is an adverb meaning with frequency

indicators.note: in means one piece is set inside the other
modified letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A loud tone changes in pitch frequency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modified' rearranges TONE to OTEN; 'in' places F inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something many times means doing it at short intervals, with frequency.

clue.text: Thus nearly all of the flower exists as a fruit

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: nearly all means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the rose is a flower
is means exists

explanation.surface: So most of the bloom survives as fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly all of' cuts the last letter from ROSE to give ROS.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically, a multiple fleshy fruit such as a mulberry or pineapple bears this name.

clue.text: Dredges enclosed parts of a river?

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
pens are fenced enclosures

explanation.surface: A question whether dredged stretches are fenced-off sections of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is the first word and the rest is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Dredging a channel makes it lower at the bottom, i.e. increases its depth.

clue.text: One who assists a superior

definitions.meaning: a helper or accomplice who gives support
read as 'a better', one who is superior

explanation.definitionFit: An abetter aids someone, and split it reads as 'a better', meaning something superior.

clue.text: Fellow gets the readings wrong for a title

parts.note: chap is an informal word for a fellow

indicators.note: set wrong, the letters of the words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A man misreads the text and ends up with the wrong book title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' is the anagram signal; 'gets' and 'for' just join the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Section headings in a book act as titles for its parts.

clue.text: Fruit is put in water

indicators.note: put in means one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: Fruit is soaked in water before cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit' and 'water' suggest soaking, but the fruit is the definition and water is rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried grape is a common fruit used in baking.

clue.text: The cooking ingredient is in the tumbler

parts.note: a tumbler is a drinking glass

explanation.surface: The ingredient for the recipe sits in the tumbler.
explanation.definitionFit: A gelatine made from fish bladders is used in cooking and in clearing wine.

clue.text: Cries the tortured unbelievers make

indicators.note: words that are tortured are twisted out of shape, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Victims of the Inquisition scream as they are tortured for their unbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'the' is fodder; 'tortured' rearranges CRIES THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who reject orthodox religious doctrine are dissenters from the faith.

clue.text: One who confiscates nothing held by devil below

indicators.note: held by means placed between, inside another piece

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
under means below
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A bailiff holds nothing, with a devil underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' means the nothing sits between the devil and the word for below.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who seizes goods or stray animals and shuts them away takes them by authority.

clue.text: Places for picking workers

parts.note: reads like a hiring hall, but means sites where fruit pickers work

explanation.definitionFit: Groves of fruit trees are where pickers gather apples and pears.

clue.text: Group I bring to court for crime

parts.note: a band is a group of people
to try a case is to bring it before a court

explanation.surface: A gang that I prosecute for lawlessness.
explanation.definitionFit: Robbery by outlaws is a form of lawbreaking.

clue.text: Part of house where one turns red during an increase of activity

indicators.note: during means the piece sits inside another, in the middle of it

parts.note: a boom is a burst of activity

indicators.note: turning the letters around gives a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Where someone blushes in the house when things get busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' is the anagram signal and 'during' the container signal; 'one' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A room for sleeping is one of the rooms of a dwelling.

clue.text: Flower gives a bribe to us

parts.note: a sop is something given to pacify or bribe

explanation.surface: Someone hands us a flower as a bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' means something that flows, a river: the Asopus is a river in Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a thing that flows, and the Asopus is a Greek watercourse.

clue.text: After a second play what is used in religion

indicators.note: after places the following piece behind the earlier ones

parts.note: a means one, written as the Roman numeral I
to strum is to play a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: After a moment, play what's used in worship.
explanation.walkthrough: An Egyptian rattle shaken in rites of Isis.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal rattle was shaken in ancient Egyptian worship of Isis.

clue.text: Lack of freedom shown in both rallies

indicators.note: shown in means the letters are displayed within the run of words

explanation.surface: Bondage is shown at both protest meetings.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in bondage or servitude is a state without liberty.

clue.text: Taking a course in entertaining?

parts.note: sounds like studying a subject at university, but means acting as host and serving guests

explanation.definitionFit: Acting as host means serving food and drink to guests, perhaps carving the course.

clue.text: People who give one a nice change

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a change of letters gives a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Folk who give someone a pleasant change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges NICE into CENI. The Iceni were an ancient British tribe led by Boudicca.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient British tribe was a people of East Anglia under Boudicca.

clue.text: Words which show that the celibate go without love

indicators.note: go without in the old sense of going outside, around another piece

parts.note: nuns are women vowed to celibacy
love is nil in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Words showing that celibates do without romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go without' means go outside, not lack: NUNS surrounds O.
explanation.definitionFit: Naming words for people, places and things are a class of words in grammar.

clue.text: Outdoor address' to writer before broadcasting

parts.note: O is the vocative used to address someone, as in O king
a pen is a writing instrument
on air means broadcasting

explanation.surface: A speech addressed to an author before it is broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held outside is in the fresh air rather than indoors.

clue.text: Apart, but see 'below

definitions.meaning: read as two words, '...', the old way of pointing to text below

explanation.definitionFit: Torn into pieces means separated, and split it reads 'as under', i.e. see below.

clue.text: Someone is confused by an understatement

indicators.note: confused letters are mixed up into another order

parts.note: split as some plus one, with one written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A person is baffled by a remark that plays things down.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Someone' as 'some one': SOME plus I. 'confused' rearranges SOME, I and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhetoric, litotes or deliberate understating is the figure called by this Greek term.

clue.text: Desire and drink get one five years

parts.note: lust is strong desire
rum is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Lust and drink land someone a five-year prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman purification held every half-decade gave its name to that period.
